newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA'S ERWIN SAYS EU TALKS LIKELY TO BE COMPLEX.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA'S ERWIN SAYS EU TALKS LIKELY TO BE COMPLEX.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin said on Wednesday South Africa's trade negotiations with the European Union were likely to be "complex and protracted".

"We have made progress in some areas and South Africa's accession to the Lome Convention is important...but we have not found each other when it comes to understanding the developmental aspects of this agreement (for the region), and we have made no progress whatsoever on agricultural products," he said during the debate on his 1997/98 budget.
Erwin cautioned that the European Union should not allow its internal politics to affect development in Southern Africa.
South Africa's limited accession to the Lome Convention was held up by objections from some members states, notably Spain, that South Africa should not be allowed to threaten producers.
Erwin said the EU wanted South Africa to make proposals on market access for industrial products, but South Africa believed it would be appropriate for the EU to make its proposals first.

This was because South Africa was working on its own proposals to the Southern African Development Community (SADC) for a free trade agreement in eight years' time which would affect its proposals to the EU.
"Our relations with the EU are of fundamental economic importance to us and they should contribute substantially to the revival of economic growth in this region," he said.
"It is our very real hope that the EU political process will not treat this negotiation as a mere trade negotiation."
